fields.body_md:
## About this programme

The Full-time MBA (Master of Business Administration) is run by Warwick Business School (WBS), a department of the University of Warwick. It is taught in English on the Warwick campus in Coventry. You can choose the 12-month format, or one of two 16-month formats: one with an internship, or one with a partner school exchange.

You study nine required modules and four or five electives, depending on the format. Core modules cover finance, marketing, operations, organisational behaviour, and digital systems and AI. You also take a required overseas elective. You can specialise in digital and AI, entrepreneurship, or social and environmental sustainability.

Check one rule before anything else. You need at least three years of professional business experience after your degree. Internships do not count.

## Can you get in?

**Your degree.** Warwick prefers a second-class honours degree (2:2) from a UK university, or an equivalent overseas degree, but does not make it essential. Warwick welcomes applications from good degrees at respected universities in India.

**Indian grades.** Warwick's India table covers Category 1 institutions: IITs, IIMs, IISERs, IIITs, NITs and other listed institutions. On courses that require a UK 2:2, the minimum is 58% (CGPA 5.8 out of 10). For other institutions, the minimum depends on the institution, so check Warwick's India page before you apply.

**Work experience.** You need at least three years of post-graduate professional business experience. Internships do not count.

**GMAT or GRE.** You need a GMAT score, a GRE score or the Warwick Test. There is no minimum score. The GMAT is a standard business school test. The GRE is a general test for graduate study. Some candidates may be offered the Warwick Test as an alternative, after interview. For reference, the class average is 670 on the GMAT (10th Edition) and 615 on the Focus Edition. A competitive GRE score is 160 in Verbal and 160 in Quant.

**Interview.** You will have an interview of about 60 minutes. It is face to face or on Microsoft Teams. It is run by Recruitment, CareersPlus or an academic.

**English.** IELTS (International English Language Testing System) is an English test. Warwick asks for IELTS Academic with an overall score of 7.0. You need at least 6.0 in each of the four parts. One-skill retakes are not accepted. Other accepted tests:

- Cambridge CPE or CAE, with 190 overall.
- PTE Academic, with 70 overall and at least 59 in each section. Take it at a test centre; online is not accepted.
- Duolingo, with 130 overall.

**Documents.** Send a digital copy of your transcript and degree certificate, translated into English. You need two professional references, one from your line manager. If you left education within the last five years, one reference can be academic and one professional.

## What it costs

Tuition is the same for UK, EU and international students. The 12-month format costs £62,500. The 16-month formats cost £63,750, which includes a £1,250 extension fee.

**Tuition deposit.** You lodge a £6,000 deposit within four weeks of receiving your offer. A deposit is an advance payment towards your tuition. It is part of the total fee, not an extra cost.

**Paying tuition.** You can pay in one lump sum at the start of the year. Or you can pay 50% on the first day of your academic year, 25% on the first day of month 4, and 25% on the first day of month 7.

**Application fee.** The application fee is £80. It is non-refundable.

**Money for the visa.** Coventry is outside London, so the outside-London rate applies. You must show £1,171 for each month of your course, for up to 9 months. You must have had this money for 28 days in a row. The end date of that 28-day period must be within 31 days of the day you apply for your visa.

**Visa and health fees.** The student visa application fee is £558 if you apply from outside the UK. You also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge: £776 for each year of your visa. You need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your course provider. The CAS is the document Warwick issues to confirm your place for the visa.

**Worked first-year total, 12-month format**

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Tuition | £62,500 |
| Money for the visa: £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Student visa application fee | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge, one year: £776 or more | £776 or more |
| **Total** | **at least £74,373** |

The sum is £62,500 + £10,539 + £558 + £776 = £74,373.

Your visa lasts longer than your course, so you usually pay for more than one year. A 16-month visa costs £1,164 in surcharge. This estimate does not include flights, rent or everyday spending.

Read how the visa works in our [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide). To compare costs at other UK universities, see the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

## Funding

**WBS Scholarships.** WBS offers scholarships for its MBA and MSc courses. UK and international students can apply. When you apply, you indicate your interest in a scholarship category on the application form.

**MBA fee scholarships.** Exceptional candidates can receive 10% to 50% of the tuition fee. For September 2027 entry, that is £6,250 to £31,250. These awards are made on an ongoing basis, so apply early.

**Scholarship categories.** On the application form, you indicate interest in a category. Examples include Change Maker, Inspiring Females, LGBTQUA+ and Locally Resident (Coventry and Warwickshire). Each category has its own rules, and India is not named in any of them.

Warwick lists all its scholarships on its [scholarships page](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/scholarships-and-bursaries/scholarships/).

## Deadlines and intakes

The intake is September 2027. The course starts on 27 September 2027.

You apply through a web-based form run by WBS. Enquiries go to warwickmba@wbs.ac.uk.

| Round | Apply by | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Round 2 | 15 November 2026 | 4 December 2026 |
| Round 3 | 10 January 2027 | 12 February 2027 |
| Round 4 | 21 March 2027 | 9 April 2027 |
| Round 5 (international deadline) | 30 May 2027 | 18 June 2027 |
| Round 6 (last round) | 1 August 2027 | 6 August 2027 |

Decisions take about four weeks.

## How to apply

1. Check that you meet the rules above, especially the three years of work experience.
2. Optional: request a consultation with WBS.
3. Apply online using the web-based form. You can save it and come back to it. The £80 application fee is non-refundable.
4. In the form, indicate your interest in a scholarship category if you want to be considered for one.
5. Upload your transcript and degree certificate, translated into English.
6. Make sure both professional references are sent.
7. Attend your interview, which takes about 60 minutes.
8. Wait for your offer letter.
9. Lodge the £6,000 deposit within four weeks of receiving your offer. Reply by the deadline in the offer letter.

## After the programme

Warwick says graduates from these courses have gone on to work for employers including Amazon, Deloitte, Goldman Sachs, HSBC, KPMG, McKinsey & Company and Unilever. CareersPlus, the careers service, offers weekly sessions and unlimited one-to-one coaching.

After the programme, you can apply for the Graduate visa. It lasts 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026. It lasts 18 months if you apply from 1 January 2027. The application fee is £937.

## Who it suits

This programme suits you if you have at least three years of professional business experience. It also suits you if you want a choice of electives and a required overseas elective. The 16-month format with an internship gives you a longer internship.

Recent classes have had students from 48 nationalities over the last three years. The class is 40% female and 60% male, and the average age is 31. The class has 70 to 100 students in two cohorts.

faq_json.q: Do I need a GMAT or GRE score for Warwick's MBA?
faq_json.a: Yes. You need a GMAT score, a GRE score or the Warwick Test. There is no minimum score. The class average is 670 on the GMAT (10th Edition) or 615 on the Focus Edition.

faq_json.q: What IELTS score does the MBA need?
faq_json.a: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, with at least 6.0 in each of the four parts. One-skill retakes are not accepted.

faq_json.q: Is the £6,000 deposit an extra cost?
faq_json.a: No. You lodge the £6,000 deposit within four weeks of receiving your offer. It is part of the total tuition fee.

faq_json.q: How much money do I need to show for the visa?
faq_json.a: Outside London, you must show £1,171 for each month of the course, for up to 9 months. That is £10,539 for 9 months. You must have had this money for 28 days in a row.

faq_json.q: When is the deadline for international applicants?
faq_json.a: The final deadline for international applicants is 30 May 2027 (Round 5). The last round is Round 6, with a deadline of 1 August 2027.
